decisions.reason: As a newly launched product in the firm's core door-hardware business, it is likely to be kept because there is no clear evidence yet of performance falling below aspiration levels and a large firm can absorb early uncertainty.
A door lever handle family fits existing capabilities and customer channels well, so absent a visible shortfall versus aspirations management would normally continue it for another year.
This design-oriented handle is somewhat more vulnerable if market acceptance lags peers, but after only one year organisational slack and limited learning time still favor retention.
Like other design variants, it may be reviewed against sales aspirations and comparable products, yet the short time since launch makes immediate withdrawal less likely than continued trial.
As another handle family closely related to the established metal-products business, it is likely to stay on the market while management gathers more evidence on demand.

The electronic access system is more distant from the firm's traditional mechanical core and therefore faces a higher risk if results disappoint, but its strategic novelty and the firm's slack make near-term continuation more likely than exit.
